definitions.explanation: A cereal grain (Hordeum vulgare) widely cultivated for food and brewing. In Japan, barley is used to make mugicha (barley tea), shochu, miso, and various foods.

examples.japanese: {大麦|おおむぎ}から{麦茶|むぎちゃ}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Barley tea is made from barley.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}では{大麦|おおむぎ}の{栽培|さいばい}が{盛|さか}んだ。
examples.english: Barley cultivation is thriving in this region.

examples.japanese: {大麦|おおむぎ}は{食物繊維|しょくもつせんい}が{豊富|ほうふ}で、{健康|けんこう}にいいと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Barley is said to be healthy because it is rich in dietary fiber.

notes:
SIMILAR WORDS:
{大麦|おおむぎ} (barley) vs {小麦|こむぎ} (wheat): Despite the names using {大|おお} (big) and {小|こ} (small), the distinction is not about size. {大麦|おおむぎ} is barley and {小麦|こむぎ} is wheat — two different grains. {麦|むぎ} alone is a general term for cereal grains.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大麦|おおむぎ}{茶|ちゃ}: barley tea (same as {麦茶|むぎちゃ})
- {大麦|おおむぎ}の{栽培|さいばい}: barley cultivation
- {大麦|おおむぎ}{若葉|わかば}: young barley grass (health supplement)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Barley has been cultivated in Japan since ancient times. It is a key ingredient in {麦茶|むぎちゃ} (barley tea, a staple summer drink), {麦|むぎ}みそ (barley miso), and {麦|むぎ}{焼酎|しょうちゅう} (barley shochu).
